MAE — Masked Image Reconstruction¶

This experiment uses a pretrained MAE model to randomly mask image patches and reconstruct the missing regions from the remaining visible patches.

1. Load the Pretrained MAE Model¶

The pretrained facebook/vit-mae-base model was loaded using ViTMAEForPreTraining. The model contains a ViT encoder and a lightweight decoder for masked image reconstruction.

In [20]:
import torch
from transformers import ViTMAEForPreTraining, ViTImageProcessor

import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
processor = ViTImageProcessor.from_pretrained("facebook/vit-mae-base")
model = ViTMAEForPreTraining.from_pretrained("facebook/vit-mae-base")

model = model.to(device)
model.eval()

2. Image Preprocessing¶

In [9]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from PIL import Image


image = Image.open("horse.jpg").convert("RGB")

print("Original size:", image.size)

plt.figure(figsize=(5, 5))
plt.imshow(image)
plt.title("Original Image")
plt.axis("off")
plt.show()

Original size: (1000, 1000)
In [10]:
inputs = processor(
    images=image,
    return_tensors="pt"
)

pixel_values = inputs["pixel_values"].to(device)

print("Input shape:", pixel_values.shape)

Input shape: torch.Size([1, 3, 224, 224])
In [11]:
import numpy as np

processed_image = pixel_values[0].permute(1, 2, 0).numpy()

mean = np.array(processor.image_mean)
std = np.array(processor.image_std)

processed_image = processed_image * std + mean
processed_image = np.clip(processed_image, 0, 1)

plt.imshow(processed_image)
plt.title("Processed Image")
plt.axis("off")
plt.show()

3. MAE Forward Pass¶

Pass the processed image through MAE. During this forward pass, the model internally performs random masking, encoder feature extraction, decoding, patch prediction, and reconstruction loss calculation.

In [12]:
with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model(pixel_values)

print("Loss:", outputs.loss.item())
print("Logits shape:", outputs.logits.shape)
print("Mask shape:", outputs.mask.shape)
print("IDs restore shape:", outputs.ids_restore.shape)

Loss: 0.13488982617855072
Logits shape: torch.Size([1, 196, 768])
Mask shape: torch.Size([1, 196])
IDs restore shape: torch.Size([1, 196])

4. Visualize the Random Mask¶

The mask generated during the MAE forward pass is converted from patch-level values back into image form.

In [ ]:
mask = outputs.mask.unsqueeze(-1)

mask = mask.repeat(
    1,
    1,
    model.config.patch_size ** 2 * 3
)

print(mask.shape)
mask = model.unpatchify(mask)
print(mask.shape)

torch.Size([1, 196, 768])
torch.Size([1, 3, 224, 224])
In [15]:
masked_image = pixel_values * (1 - mask)
mean = np.array(processor.image_mean)
std = np.array(processor.image_std)

def tensor_to_image(tensor):

    img = tensor.detach().cpu()[0]
    img = img.permute(1, 2, 0).numpy()

    img = img * std + mean

    img = np.clip(img, 0, 1)

    return img


masked_show = tensor_to_image(masked_image)

plt.figure(figsize=(6, 6))

plt.imshow(masked_show)
plt.title("Masked Image (75%)")
plt.axis("off")

plt.show()

5. Visualize the MAE Prediction¶

The decoder output outputs.logits contains the predicted pixel values for the image patches.

In [17]:
prediction = model.unpatchify(outputs.logits)

print(prediction.shape)

prediction_show = tensor_to_image(prediction)

plt.figure(figsize=(6, 6))

plt.imshow(prediction_show)
plt.title("MAE Prediction")
plt.axis("off")

plt.show()

torch.Size([1, 3, 224, 224])

6. Reconstruct the Image¶

In [18]:
reconstruction = (
    pixel_values * (1 - mask)
    + prediction * mask
)

reconstruction_show = tensor_to_image(reconstruction)

plt.figure(figsize=(6, 6))

plt.imshow(reconstruction_show)
plt.title("MAE Reconstruction")
plt.axis("off")

plt.show()

7. Compare the Results¶

The original image, masked image, MAE prediction, and final reconstruction are displayed together for comparison.

Original → Masked (75%) → MAE Prediction → Reconstruction

In [19]:
original_show = tensor_to_image(pixel_values)
masked_show = tensor_to_image(masked_image)
prediction_show = tensor_to_image(prediction)
reconstruction_show = tensor_to_image(reconstruction)

plt.figure(figsize=(16, 4))

plt.subplot(1, 4, 1)
plt.imshow(original_show)
plt.title("Original")
plt.axis("off")

plt.subplot(1, 4, 2)
plt.imshow(masked_show)
plt.title("Masked (75%)")
plt.axis("off")

plt.subplot(1, 4, 3)
plt.imshow(prediction_show)
plt.title("MAE Prediction")
plt.axis("off")

plt.subplot(1, 4, 4)
plt.imshow(reconstruction_show)
plt.title("Reconstruction")
plt.axis("off")

plt.show()

Conclusion¶

Despite having 75% of the patches masked, MAE reconstructs the overall structure of the horse and the surrounding scene. The reconstructed regions are more blurred than the original image, but the main semantic and spatial information remains recognizable.

This experiment demonstrates how MAE learns visual representations through masked image reconstruction. The encoder processes only the visible patches, while the decoder uses the encoded representations to predict the missing image regions.
